The Verses of the Elder Gayākassapa:
“Three times a day— at dawn, at midday, and at evening— I [meditate].”
At Gayā, on the full moon day of Phagguṇa, I bathed in the waters of the Otalā.
Whatever evil I have committed—
‘In former lives,
I shall now cast that away here’—
such was the view I held previously.
Having heard well-spoken words,
phrases endowed with the meaning of the Dhamma,
which are true and accordant with reality—
I have reflected with wise discernment.
All evil has been washed away;
I am stainless, purified, and pure.
Pure, he is the heir of the pure one;
a son born from the breast of the Buddha.
Having plunged into the stream of the Eightfold Path,
I have washed away all evil;
I have attained the threefold knowledge;
the teaching of the Buddha has been accomplished.
… the Elder Gayākassapa …
